title: AETHERIA 2099 — a cyberpunk text adventure built with AI in the loop (free demo)
author: K_kkomi
selftext:
\*\*Free browser demo (\~15 min, no sign-up):\*\* [https://k-kom.itch.io/aetheria-2099](https://k-kom.itch.io/aetheria-2099)



AETHERIA 2099 is a cyberpunk text adventure. You're Jayne, a memory broker in a domed city where an AI called NEXUS holds everyone's memories. A dying courier hands you a chip nobody can price, and three people want it: a broker who prices everything, a Guard officer hiding behind regulations, and a pirate broadcaster who wants to wake the city up.



Every choice gets its own written response, and you can also type your own line instead of clicking. Something you learn on one run unlocks a new option on the next. The demo covers one of three paths; the full game is planned as a paid release.



\*\*How AI was used.\*\* My first plan was a fine-tuned 7B model narrating the game live. It scored 91.8% on my eval and the text was unreadable, so I dropped that. Now the scenes are drafted with a larger model (Claude) ahead of time and revised together: I decide the characters, what each path costs, and what isn't working. The small model only interprets what you type. Most of the code was also written by an AI coding assistant while I directed and tested, and the English and intro video are AI-generated.



Curious how others here handle this: do you keep generation at authoring time, or have you made runtime generation work for narrative?

comments.author: K_kkomi
comments.body: If anyone does try the demo, I'd really like to hear three things: where you stopped, whether any choice felt like it actually mattered, and what you typed into the free-text box and whether the reply made sense. That last one is the part I can't test properly on my own — I only think like one player. Comments here or on the itch page both work, and I read all of them.
